name: TE Connectivity plc

profile.description: TE Connectivity plc is the world's largest connector and sensor company. It designs and makes connectivity and sensor solutions for harsh environments in two segments: Transportation Solutions (automotive connectors, electrification components, industrial and commercial transportation, sensors) and Industrial Solutions (digital data networks for AI data centers, aerospace, defense, medical, automation, and energy/grid). Fiscal 2026 sales were about $19.9B, up about 15%, and orders hit a record $22.2B.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Over five years TE has extended its connector leadership into AI data-center interconnect, grid modernization and vehicle electrification. Fiscal Q4 2026 sales reached a record $5.3B (up 12% reported, 13% organic) and full-year sales grew about 15% [1][2]. This is consistent execution in new secular markets rather than a transformative pivot. AI Deployment (1/2): CEO Terrence Curtin frames AI as long-term transformation rather than short-term efficiency [6], and AI connectivity is a named growth vector [5]. TE has not quantified internal AI savings. Market Share (2/2): TE is the world's largest connector company. Q4 orders of $6.1B rose 29% YoY, and full-year orders of $22.2B rose 27%, showing share momentum in data-center and grid end markets [1][2]. Pipeline (2/2): Q1 FY2027 guidance is about $5.35B in sales (up 15%), and management expects strong double-digit growth in fiscal 2027 backed by the record order book [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D was $829M, about 4.8% of sales and rising from $718M in FY2022 [12], at the top of the passive-component and connector peer range.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): TE's purpose, to create a safer, sustainable, productive and connected future, is specific and links engineering precision to societal outcomes. Leadership uses it in strategic messaging about AI, grid and electrification growth vectors [5][7]. Community Impact (1/2): TE runs corporate giving and sustainability programs, holds a Low Risk Sustainalytics rating of 11.2 [10], and has been recognized for its ESG policies [11]. The searches surfaced no distinctive foundation programs with dollar amounts. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found. A third-party summary describes engineering-led direction but uneven middle-management execution that varies by plant and region [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): The research found no meaningful net insider buying in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically as a Dividend stock (sleeve forced from IOWN holdings) [12]. D/E of 41.1% scores 1.0, ROE of 24.6% scores 1.0, FY2026 revenue growth of about 15% scores 1.0 [1], and forward P/E of 14.7 scores 1.0. Five-year revenue CAGR of about 5.9% (FY2021 $14.9B to FY2026 about $19.9B) scores 0.73, and profit margin of 16.4% scores 0.82. These are the only drags. On dividends, the 28.5% payout ratio scores 1.0, 19 consecutive years paid since the 2007 Tyco separation scores 1.0 at 2x, about 14 years of increases scores 1.0, and the 5-year dividend CAGR of about 9.3% ($0.50 to $0.78 quarterly) scores 1.0 at 2x. Weighted sum 11.55 / 12 = 9.62, which rounds to 10. Liquidity floor cleared at about $448M of daily dollar volume.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): TE makes physical connectors, cable assemblies and sensors that every AI server, GPU rack, switch and power system needs. Software cannot substitute for them, and AI build-outs increase unit demand. AI data-center connectivity and grid modernization are among the growth vectors behind record orders of $22.2B, up 27% [1][5]. AI Opportunity (1/1): TE earns quantifiable AI revenue through its Digital Data Networks business, whose AI-driven orders have been a leading contributor to the 29% Q4 order growth [1][3].

infinite_game.summary: TE has a credible purpose and a CEO, Terrence Curtin (CEO since 2017), who publicly argues for long-term AI transformation over short-term efficiency [6]. It has also steadily reallocated its portfolio toward secular growth markets. Through Sinek's lens, however, TE is an excellent operator rather than a cause-driven company: its narrative centers on orders, margins and EPS growth, and there is limited evidence of a Circle of Safety or an infinite competitive mindset.

just_cause.analysis: (2/3) TE's goal of a safer, sustainable, productive and connected future is distinctive for a component maker, and leadership ties capital allocation to it through AI, grid and electrification vectors [5][7]. It has not yet been tested across a CEO transition or a long downturn.

trusting_teams.analysis: (1/2) Leadership has been stable, with Curtin as CEO since 2017 [7]. Corporate materials stress engagement and inclusion, but third-party employee summaries describe uneven middle management and slower decisions at the plant level [4], so trust is adequate rather than exceptional.

worthy_rivals.analysis: (0/1) Public commentary centers on share gains, record orders and margin expansion. TE also had litigation over active electrical cables with Credo that was settled in March 2026 [9]. No management commentary frames rivals as teachers.

existential_flexibility.analysis: (1/2) TE has steadily reshaped its portfolio, for example exiting the SubCom undersea business and leaning into data-center and energy connectivity [1][5]. These are incremental shifts within connectivity, not a reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: (1/2) TE kept R&D rising from $718M in FY2022 to $829M in FY2025 through soft automotive and industrial markets [12]. Curtin also argues publicly against treating AI as a short-term cost-cutting tool [6]. Both are evidence of choosing long-term capability.

investment_thesis: TE closed fiscal 2026 with record Q4 sales of $5.3B (up 12%), more than 20% adjusted EPS growth, and record full-year orders of $22.2B (up 27%), giving it momentum into a guided 15% sales increase in Q1 FY2027 [1][2]. As the largest connector maker, it sells into AI data centers, grid modernization and vehicle electrification. The balance sheet is strong (41% D/E, 24.6% ROE), and the stock trades at only 14.7x forward earnings with a PEG of 0.95 [12]. The dividend has compounded at about 9% a year with a sub-30% payout ratio.
thesis_continued: The main risk is cyclical. Transportation Solutions is still TE's largest segment and depends on global auto production, which faces EV-adoption uncertainty and tariff disruption, including an $87M IEEPA tariff refund obligation in Q4 [3]. TTM book-to-bill of about 1.12 is healthy but not exceptional, and AI data-center orders could prove lumpy if hyperscaler capex pauses. The 16.4% profit margin trails top-tier peers, and the -49 Inspire score is a values flag for faith-based investors.
key_catalysts: Conversion of record $22.2B FY2026 orders into the guided 15% Q1 FY2027 sales growth and double-digit FY2027 growth [1]
Further AI data-center interconnect orders (Digital Data Networks) and grid/energy connectivity demand [1][5]
Margin expansion and buybacks supporting continued 20%+ adjusted EPS growth at a 14.7x forward P/E [2][12]
key_risks: Global light-vehicle production slowdown or EV program delays hitting Transportation Solutions, still TE's largest segment
Hyperscaler capex digestion causing AI connectivity orders to decelerate from 2026's elevated levels
Tariff and trade-policy volatility, including IEEPA refund pass-throughs that reduced reported Q4 growth [3]

backlog.note: FY2026 orders reached a record $22.2B (up 27%) against about $19.9B of sales, for a TTM book-to-bill of about 1.12. Q4 orders of $6.1B rose 29% YoY with a 1.14 book-to-bill. Order growth is accelerating, led by AI data-center (DDN) and energy connectivity. TE does not disclose a total backlog figure [1].
